equipment_type: Kitchen hood demand ventilation controller (exhaust and make-up air fans)
applies_to: The main BACnet device of a Melink Intelli-Hood 3 (IH3 SC) kitchen demand-control ventilation system.
summary: The Intelli-Hood IH3 System Controller is the main BACnet IP device of the older Intelli-Hood 3 kitchen ventilation system and a virtual router for the fan and hood devices behind it. Its own object list is small and read-only: the state of three digital inputs, two dry-contact outputs, two 24 VDC outputs, and the analog input and output as a percentage. It differs from the IH4 System Controller (three inputs here instead of four, and only one analog input and output).
notes: All objects are Binary Values or Analog Values and read-only.

What each input or output does (Remote On/Off, Remote Enable/Disable, Fan On, Temperature Alarm, Smoke, MUA Damper and so on) is set in the Intelli-Hood configuration; the objects only show the contact state.
The exhaust fan, auxiliary airflow, hood controller and virtual I/O devices of the IH3 have the same object lists as the IH4 versions already in this library.
Supported BIBBs: DS-RP-B, DS-RPM-B, DS-WP-B, DM-DDB-B, DM-DOB-B; B-ASC profile, no segmentation.

source.title: Intelli-Hood BACnet Protocol Implementation Conformance Statement (PICS), Version 8.0

integration.summary: Discover the System Controller (default Device ID 654000), then the fan and hood devices through its virtual router. This device only reports the state of its physical I/O; map the outputs set up as Fan On or alarms and the inputs wired for remote on/off or enable.

integration.enable: No BACnet enable or start/stop object on this device. Fans start from the Touchpad, schedules or digital inputs (physical, or the Virtual Input Module over BACnet).
integration.heartbeat: The BACnet Watchdog (0-600 s, default 300 s, 0 = off) on the System Controller resets all Virtual Input Module inputs when no BACnet traffic addressed to the Intelli-Hood arrives in time.
setup: Main BACnet IP device, default Device ID 654000, UDP port 47808; virtual router with default DNET 654 for the other devices.
With BACnet Auto Number on, the fan and hood devices are numbered sequentially after the System Controller's Device ID.
Settings are made on the Touchpad (System Configuration, unlocked by holding Up and Down for ten seconds), the web configurator or a USB configuration file.
gotchas: The DNET must be unique on the BACnet network, or the virtual devices become unreachable.
Front ends that do not discover through routers only find the System Controller.
All objects here are read-only; fans cannot be commanded from this device.
